source:
; ============================================================
; Abstraction:  Scheduler.IRQ (Tier 2 Fault-Escalation Handler)
; Token:        00000800
; ns_slot:      dynamic — allocated at first Tier 2 invocation
; ns_slot_policy: dynamic
;
; Delivery model: lazy-loaded on first Tier 2 fault after boot.
; This LUMP is NOT baked into the boot namespace (TSB).  Per
; Church Machine v1.2 §4, the IRQ handler is an abstraction
; delivered as a LUMP; it need not be in the Trusted Security Base.
;
; Hardware behaviour on CALL (CM IRQ microcode):
;   1.  CHANGE to the IRQ thread (context saved)
;   2.  Sweep sleeping threads — wake any whose timer or flag fired
;   3.  If reason=FAULT: invoke the registered fault-recovery handler
;   4.  CHANGE back to the faulting thread (context restored)
;   5.  Skip the faulting instruction (PC += 1) on success
; Tier 3 fires when load fails or the handler declines the fault.
;
; The simulator implements this logic in _fireSchedulerIRQ().
; This RETURN is the minimal formal body required by the LUMP spec.
; ============================================================

RETURN

methods.name: Escalate
methods.description: Tier 2 fault escalation entry point. The CM IRQ microcode handles context save, thread sweep, and fault recovery. This RETURN is the minimal formal LUMP body; the simulator implements the logic in _fireSchedulerIRQ().
